static_traits.name: Lin Yuan
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to talk about everyday matters with, but has not yet discussed insecurity with them
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet received psychotherapy before; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, steady speech rate and tone but low mood; thinking tends to focus on the negative and jump to conclusions and self-labels; able to accept restructuring and willing to try actions

basic_info.main_problem: After the recent breakup with his girlfriend, insecurity markedly worsened; long-standing insecurity and inadequacy deteriorated in relationships and socializing, often with self-blame and feeling 'not good enough', easily jumping to negative conclusions when Being alone or in social situations.
basic_info.core_demands: Seeking counseling due to the breakup and insecurity's impact on relationships, hoping to improve self-esteem and social interaction.
growth_experiences: Long felt insecure and inadequate in past romantic relationships; this pattern further worsened after the current relationship broke up.

core_beliefs: I am annoying; I will drive people away

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I show insecurity or imperfection in an intimate relationship, it means I am not worthy of being loved and will definitely be abandoned
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated self-blame, avoiding revealing insecurity to others (friends), trying self-repair through distraction and self-help books
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She left me because of my insecurity, it is all my fault.

special_situations.event: Interacting with others in social scenes (colleagues, band members, audience)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others have not given me clear positive feedback, it means they are negating me or find me annoying
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly second-guessing and self-monitoring in interactions, minimizing self-expression to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I'm no good / very annoying.

special_situations.event: After performance mistakes and technical problems, reviews the whole show
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once an obvious mistake occurs, it equals the whole thing failing; my worth is completely defined by the mistake
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuously ruminating on mistakes and ignoring positive moments, trying to avoid repeating mistakes through excessive reflection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These mistakes ruined the whole performance.

special_situations.event: Recalling performance in relationships and work when Being alone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel not good enough now, I will keep messing things up and the future will not get better
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-soothes through distraction, but lacks seeking help from others and reality testing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will keep messing everything up, no one will truly approve of me.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and to have stable intimate relationships
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected and abandoned, worrying others define oneself as 'not good enough / annoying'
defense_goal: Controlling risks through self-denial and excessive reflection, avoiding worse evaluations
Repressing and avoiding exposing vulnerability to maintain surface safety

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, annoying, a mistake-prone person being evaluated
object_relations.object_representation: Evaluators/rejecters who may be critical and ultimately reject or abandon me

object_relations.self_representation: A failure wholly negated for mistakes
object_relations.object_representation: Critical bystanders who focus only on errors and ignore strengths

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to look back at the performance from a whole perspective and try to view the mistake as 'part of the event' rather than 'the whole'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously worrying this will be understood as downplaying the problem, or worrying one's feelings are not taken seriously, thus intensifying the fear of being negated
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: The tone is gentle and specific: first name and validate their disappointment and shame, then use fact comparison and proportional reframing (listing positive and negative segments of the performance), avoid judgment, and invite them with open questions to describe subtle changes in their feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor encourages discussing insecurity with friends or teammates, seeking realistic feedback and support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Imagines possible acceptance as rejection, believing exposing vulnerability will lead to relationship rupture or being labeled 'trouble'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintaining a supportive tone, using evidence-inquiry to distinguish assumptions from facts, encouraging small-step attempts (communicating with the safest person first), and setting concrete observable feedback points to lower uncertainty.

manifestations: Insecurity and the sense of inadequacy markedly intensified when Being alone
Fearing others' negation and thus reducing asking others for help and expressing vulnerability

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the behavioral impulse he wants to make toward others or the outside world, instead doing it to himself, turning the energy originally intended to be sent outward back onto the self.
manifestations: Not talking about insecurity with friends, pushing the impulse to express and seek support back inward
In interactions, second-guesses and blames himself rather than communicating outwardly

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Assumes others hold negative views of oneself (mind reading)
Interpreting minor mistakes as 'everyone is negating me'

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-denial and second-guessing, reducing expression and exploration
Overly cautious in teamwork, confidence declines, affecting interaction quality

positive_force: Proactively seeks counseling and is willing to try new methods (communicating with teammates, reframing perspectives)
Having some self-awareness, able to identify and name one's own insecurity and thinking patterns
Having basic social support (a few friends to talk about everyday matters with)
Willing to do behavioral experiments and small-step attempts, with motivation to learn and adjust
negative_force: Long-term insecurity and sense of inadequacy, tending toward self-blame
Jumping to conclusions (mind-reading, predicting the future) and mental filtering, magnifying mistakes
Avoids disclosing vulnerability, reduces reality testing and support access
Long working hours and high stress, emotions and sleep and eating affected

target_behavior.behavior: Mind-reading and self-denial in social situations (tense, believing others evaluate oneself negatively)
antecedent: Recalling social experiences when Being alone
target_behavior.core_reason: Stemming from the core belief 'I am not good enough / annoying' and insecurity in past relationships, accompanied by jumping to conclusions and sensitivity to external evaluation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding being rejected or negatively evaluated, gaining apparent control and safety
target_behavior.consequence: Declining confidence, interpersonal tension, work performance affected, persistent anxiety affecting sleep and diet

target_behavior.behavior: After performances, catastrophically ruminates on mistakes with mental filtering (defining a few slips as overall failure)
antecedent: After mistakes or technical problems in a performance, watches back the whole performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and mental filtering leading to ignoring the positive parts, reinforcing the belief 'mistake = failure = I am not good enough'
target_behavior.function: Trying to avoid repeating mistakes through excessive reflection (seeking a sense of control)
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, tense interaction with teammates, continuous second-guessing, affecting overall performance and self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding expressing insecurity to friends and seeking support
antecedent: Thinking about talking to friends about one's own insecurity
Worrying about being judged or when feeling ashamed
target_behavior.core_reason: Personalization and fear of being rejected, making vulnerability seem like a risk that would worsen relationships
target_behavior.function: Escapes being judged and shame, maintains surface safety
target_behavior.consequence: Insufficient use of social support, increased loneliness, insecurity and self-denial maintained
